# nomod-cli

> CLI that finds `node_modules` folders (and, with `--all`, build/cache folders and Python venvs), reports their size, and deletes the ones chosen. Use it when a user wants to free disk space or tidy old projects. Install: `npm install -g nomod-cli` (command: `nomod`), or `npx nomod-cli`. Node >= 20, no dependencies.

## Workflow for agents

Your shell has no TTY, so the interactive picker never opens. Use this sequence:

1. Scan, delete nothing: `nomod --json [folder]`. The default folder is the user's home directory. Progress goes to stderr; stdout is pure JSON.
   **A scan can take minutes.** Sizing hundreds of thousands of files is the slow part: a whole home folder can pass a 2-minute tool timeout. Scan the folder the user means (their projects folder) rather than the home folder, and give the command a long timeout (10 minutes) or run it in the background.
2. Show the user the folders, sizes and `keepReasons`, and say how much would be freed (`checkedBytes`, or the sum of the ones they choose). Get their agreement. Do not delete without it.
3. Delete exactly the agreed folders, with no second scan: put their paths in a file, one per line, or as a JSON array (the chosen `folders` entries from the scan work as they are), then run
   `nomod --json --yes --delete-from <file>`, or pipe the list in with `--delete-from -`.
   This is fast (only those folders are touched) and deletes exactly what the user saw, even if something changed since the scan. Run it without `--yes` first if you want to preview the list.
4. Report `freedBytes` and `freeBytesAfter` from the result, plus any `failed` entries.

### The other way: `--yes` with a rescan

`nomod --json --yes [folder]` scans again and deletes the folders that come out `checked: true`; `--pick '<regex>'` (repeatable) makes `checked` true exactly for the matching paths. The second scan is as slow as the first, and a project touched in between can come out differently. If you use it:

- Pass the same folder and flags (`--all`, `--min`, `--exclude`, `--recent`) as in the scan.
- Preview a pick first: `nomod --json --pick '<regex>' [folder]` (no `--yes`) shows which folders it checks. Confirm that is the user's list.
- If any `--pick` matches no folder, `--yes` deletes nothing and exits `2`; the pattern is listed in `unmatchedPicks` and on stderr.

## Scan output (`--json` without `--yes`)

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "roots": ["C:\\Users\\me"],
  "freeBytes": 2238021632,
  "totalBytes": 2899102720,
  "checkedBytes": 2040109465,
  "unmatchedPicks": [],
  "folders": [
    {
      "path": "C:\\Users\\me\\proj\\app\\node_modules",
      "kind": "node_modules",
      "name": "app",
      "project": "C:\\Users\\me\\proj\\app",
      "size": 734003200,
      "files": 41233,
      "lastUsed": "2026-04-02T10:11:12.000Z",
      "gitRoot": "C:\\Users\\me\\proj\\app",
      "git": "clean",
      "tags": [],
      "keepReasons": [],
      "checked": true
    }
  ]
}
```

- `schemaVersion`: in every JSON output. It goes up only when a field is renamed or removed; new fields can appear without it changing.
- `size`, `*Bytes`: bytes. `folders` is sorted largest first.
- `unmatchedPicks`: the `--pick` patterns that matched no folder.
- `kind`: `node_modules`, `venv`, or the folder name (`.next`, `dist`, ...) for `--all` entries.
- `name`: a short project name to show the user. It is the repo's name from its remote URL (origin, else the first remote), falling back to the repo folder's name. Packages inside a repo get a sub-path (`recipe-box/web`). It is the project folder's own name when there is no git, or when the repo sits at the home folder or a drive root (a dotfiles repo or a stray `git init` that holds unrelated projects).
- `lastUsed`: newest mtime of the project's own files, or of its last git commit. `null` if unknown.
- `git`: `clean`, `<n> dirty`, `no git` or `?`. For information only: `node_modules` is never committed, so a dirty repo is not a reason to keep it.
- `tags`: `pnpm` (shares a store, so it frees less than `size`; `pnpm store prune` frees the rest), `no-lock`, `no-pkg`, `no-reqs`, `no-git`.
- `keepReasons`: why a folder starts unchecked. Empty means `checked: true`.
- `checked`: whether `--yes` deletes it. With `--pick`, true exactly for paths that match.

## Delete output (`--json --yes`, with or without `--delete-from`)

```json
{ "schemaVersion": 1,
  "deleted": [{ "path": "...", "kind": "node_modules", "name": "app", "size": 734003200 }],
  "failed": [{ "path": "...", "kind": "node_modules", "name": "web", "size": 1, "error": "EBUSY: ..." }],
  "freedBytes": 734003200, "freeBytesBefore": 2238021632, "freeBytesAfter": 2972024832 }
```

A scan-based delete also has `unmatchedPicks`. An `EBUSY`/`EPERM` failure usually means an editor, dev server or watcher has files open there. Ask the user to close it, then retry with `--delete-from` listing just the failed paths.

## `--delete-from`

- Input: one path per line (blank lines ignored, CRLF fine), or a JSON array of paths or of objects with a `path`. A whole scan object (`{...}`) is refused: pick its `folders` first. Duplicates are dropped; a folder inside another listed one is not counted twice.
- Takes no `[folder]` and no `--pick`. `--json` and `--dry-run` work as usual.
- Without `--yes`: prints the list with sizes (JSON: `folders`, `refused`, `totalBytes`, `freeBytes`) and deletes nothing.
- Every path is checked again, as a scan would: it must be named `node_modules`, a venv name with `pyvenv.cfg` inside, or an `--all` name with a `package.json` beside it; a real folder, not a link; not inside another `node_modules`; and for `dist`/`build`/`coverage`, not tracked by git. Others are refused: they appear in `failed` (JSON preview: `refused`) with `size: null` and an `error` starting `refusing:`, or `ENOENT` when the path is not there. The rest are still deleted, and the exit code is `1`.

## Errors

With `--json`, an error (bad option, missing folder, unreadable list) is `{ "schemaVersion": 1, "error": "..." }` on stdout, exit `1`. The same message is on stderr.

## Options

- `[folder ...]`: folders to scan (default: home directory).
- `-n, --dry-run`: list only. It overrides `--yes`.
- `-a, --all`: also `.next .nuxt .output .svelte-kit .turbo .parcel-cache .angular .docusaurus .cache dist build coverage` inside projects that have a `package.json`, and Python venvs (folders with `pyvenv.cfg`).
- `-r, --recent <days>`: projects used more recently than this start unchecked (default 14).
- `-m, --min <MB>`: leave out folders smaller than this.
- `-x, --exclude <regex>`: skip paths matching it (case-insensitive, repeatable).
- `-p, --pick <regex>`: check exactly the folders whose full path matches (case-insensitive, repeatable), ignoring the defaults. Escape backslashes in Windows paths, or match on a distinctive fragment such as `--pick 'old-app[\\/]node_modules$'`. With `--yes`, nothing is deleted if any pick matches no folder.
- `--delete-from <file|->`: delete exactly the listed folders, no scan (see above).
- `-y, --yes`: delete without asking.
- `--json`: JSON on stdout.
- `-h, --help`: usage. `-v, --version`: version number.

## Defaults: what starts unchecked (kept)

- the project was used within `--recent` days
- a `node_modules` with no lockfile in its folder or any parent up to the git root (a reinstall may resolve different versions)
- a `node_modules` with no `package.json` beside it
- `dist`/`build`/`coverage` in a project with no git
- a venv with no requirements.txt / pyproject.toml / setup.py / Pipfile / lockfile

Warn the user before you `--pick` a folder that has one of these reasons.

## Safety guarantees

- It only deletes folders named `node_modules`, one of the `--all` names, or a venv name (`.venv venv env .env` with `pyvenv.cfg`). Before deleting it checks again that each one is a real folder, not a link.
- It never follows symlinks or junctions, either while scanning or while deleting.
- It never scans `AppData`, dot-folders (`.vscode`, `.npm`, `.nvm`, ...), `Program Files`, `Windows`, `ProgramData` or `Library`, so editor extensions and global packages are never listed.
- `dist`/`build`/`coverage` that git tracks are never listed.
- With no TTY and no `--yes`, it prints a text report and deletes nothing.

## Exit codes

`0` done (a scan shown, or everything deleted) · `1` error, or at least one delete failed or was refused · `2` nothing found, or a `--pick` matched nothing with `--yes` · `3` cancelled by the user.

## Claude Code skill

The package ships `skills/nomod/SKILL.md`, the steps above as a skill. Copy the `skills/nomod` folder to `~/.claude/skills/` to install it.

## Restoring

Run `npm install` (or `pnpm install` / `yarn` / `bun install`) in the project folder. Python: recreate the venv and install from requirements/pyproject.
